alalal-e84949-d1e101.summary: Rubric marking the division of Lombard's text for Distinction 24 of Book III.

alalal-e84949-d1e106.summary: Introduces the part beginning 'If faith is only of things not seen, how does Truth say to the Apostles...', which treats objections against the last part of the Apostle's definition of faith expounded in the previous distinction.

alalal-e84949-d1e127.summary: Divides the part in two: whether the same thing can be seen and believed, and whether the same thing can be known and believed ('Post haec quaeri solet').

alalal-e84949-d1e146.summary: Divides the first into two: Lombard shows generally that faith is not of things seen or proved; then he solves the special difficulty about the article of the passion, since the Apostles saw Christ suffer and yet believed ('Si vero quaeritur, utrum Petrus').
concepts: faith not of things seen or proved

alalal-e84949.summary: Division of Lombard's text for Distinction 24, which answers objections to the claim, from Hebrews 11:1, that faith concerns things not apparent. Lombard asks whether the same thing can be both seen and believed, showing generally that faith is not of things seen or proved and treating the Apostles, who saw Christ suffer yet believed. He then asks whether the same thing can be both known and believed.
